P.title: P.blurb
Generative AI: How models that write, draw and talk work, and how to use them well.

P.title: gen-what.summary
Generative AI: Models that create text, images, sound and code.

P.title: gen-what.q0.o1
Generative AI: It creates new content rather than only classifying

P.title: gen-what.q0.x
Generative AI: It generates text, images, code or sound.

P.title: gen-what.q1.q
Generative AI: A model adapted to many tasks after broad training is called…

P.title: gen-what.q2.q
Generative AI: Which is a weakness of generative AI?

P.title: gen-what.c0.text
Generative AI: Classic AI mostly classifies and predicts: is this spam, what will demand be? Generative AI creates new content: a paragraph, an image, a melody, a piece of code, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of examples.

P.title: gen-what.c1.text
Generative AI: Most generative models learn the probability of data: which word tends to follow which, which pixels look like a cat. Generating means sampling from that learned distribution, one piece at a time.

P.title: gen-what.c2.text
Generative AI: Large models trained on broad data, then adapted to many tasks, are called foundation models. One model can summarise, translate, write code and answer questions without being retrained for each.

P.title: gen-what.c3.text
Generative AI: Large language models generate text and code. Diffusion models generate images and video. Other models generate speech, music and 3D. Increasingly, one multimodal model handles several.

P.title: gen-what.c4.text
Generative AI: Image generators (DALL·E 2, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion) and ChatGPT all broke through in 2022. Within months, hundreds of millions of people were using generative AI.

P.title: gen-what.c5.text
Generative AI: Generative AI shines at first drafts, summarising, rewriting, translating, brainstorming, explaining, extracting information from messy documents and writing routine code.

P.title: gen-what.c6.text
Generative AI: It isn't a database of facts or a calculator. It can be confidently wrong, has knowledge cutoffs and doesn't know your private data unless you provide it.

P.title: gen-what.c7.text
Generative AI: A chatbot app (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot) is a product built around a model, with a chat interface, safety layers, memory, tools and file handling. The same model can power many different products.

P.title: gen-what.c8.text
Generative AI: The most effective use pairs AI speed with human judgement: AI drafts, a person checks facts, adds context and decides. You stay responsible for the output.

P.title: gen-what.c9.text
Generative AI: Generative AI changes knowledge work the way spreadsheets changed accounting: many tasks get faster, new tasks appear, and skills like judgement and clear thinking become more valuable.

P.title: gen-llm.q0.q
Generative AI: What is an LLM trained to do during pre-training?

P.title: gen-llm.q1.q
Generative AI: What turns a base model into an assistant?

P.title: gen-llm.q2.q
Generative AI: About how many English words are in 1,000 tokens?

P.title: gen-llm.q2.x
Generative AI: Roughly ¾ of a word per token.

P.title: gen-llm.c0.text
Generative AI: An LLM is trained on one task: predict the next token in a text. Done across trillions of tokens, this forces the model to absorb grammar, facts, reasoning patterns and styles.

P.title: gen-llm.c1.text
Generative AI: Text is split into tokens, roughly ¾ of an English word each. Models read and produce tokens, and usage is priced and limited in tokens. Portuguese usually needs a few more tokens than English for the same content.

P.title: gen-llm.c2.text
Generative AI: Pre-training uses huge datasets: web pages, books, code, scientific papers and more, filtered for quality. Frontier models train on many trillions of tokens.

P.title: gen-llm.c3.text
Generative AI: Training a frontier model uses thousands of GPUs for weeks or months and costs tens to hundreds of millions of dollars. That's why only a handful of labs train the largest models.

P.title: gen-llm.c4.text
Generative AI: Researchers found that loss falls predictably as you scale parameters, data and compute together. This gave labs confidence to build ever larger models.

P.title: gen-llm.c5.text
Generative AI: A base model just continues text; ask it a question and it might write more questions. Instruction tuning and preference training turn it into a helpful assistant that follows requests.

P.title: gen-llm.c6.text
Generative AI: The base model is fine-tuned on many examples of instructions paired with good responses: "Summarise this", "Write an email", "Explain like I'm 10".

P.title: gen-llm.c7.text
Generative AI: People (and AI critics) compare pairs of responses and pick the better one. A reward model learns these preferences, and the assistant is trained to score well: RLHF, or related methods like RLAIF and DPO.

P.title: gen-llm.c8.text
Generative AI: Newer models are trained to think step by step before answering, spending more computation on hard problems. This "test-time compute" improves maths, coding and planning.

P.title: gen-llm.c9.text
Generative AI: A model's knowledge stops at the end of its training data. It won't know later events unless given tools like web search or documents you provide.

P.title: gen-transformer.q0.q
Generative AI: What does attention let a token do?

P.title: gen-transformer.q0.o1
Generative AI: Weigh how relevant every other token is to its meaning

P.title: gen-transformer.q0.x
Generative AI: It blends information from relevant tokens.

P.title: gen-transformer.q2.q
Generative AI: How does attention cost grow with context length n?

P.title: gen-transformer.q2.x
Generative AI: Every token compares with every other.

P.title: gen-transformer.c0.text
Generative AI: Earlier language models (RNNs, LSTMs) read text one word at a time, passing a memory along. They struggled with long texts and couldn't be trained in parallel efficiently.

P.title: gen-transformer.c1.text
Generative AI: Attention lets each token look at every other token and decide which matter for its meaning. In "The bank raised rates", "bank" attends to "rates" and means a financial bank.

P.title: gen-transformer.c1.viz.steps.1
Generative AI: Compares with every other token's key

P.title: gen-transformer.c2.text
Generative AI: Each token produces three vectors: a query (what am I looking for?), a key (what do I offer?) and a value (my information). Matching queries to keys decides how much of each value to take.

P.title: gen-transformer.c3.text
Generative AI: Models run many attention "heads" in parallel. Different heads learn to track different relationships: grammar, who-did-what, references to earlier names, formatting.

P.title: gen-transformer.c4.text
Generative AI: A Transformer stacks dozens of layers, each with attention plus a feed-forward network. Early layers handle surface patterns; deeper layers build abstract meaning.

P.title: gen-transformer.c5.text
Generative AI: Attention alone doesn't know word order. Position information is added to each token so "dog bites man" differs from "man bites dog".

P.title: gen-transformer.c5.viz.l.items.0
Generative AI: dog bites man = man bites dog

P.title: gen-transformer.c6.text
Generative AI: Transformers process all tokens in parallel, which suits GPUs perfectly. That made it practical to train on vastly more data, the key to today's capabilities.

P.title: gen-transformer.c7.text
Generative AI: Standard attention compares every token with every other, so cost grows with the square of context length. Engineering tricks and new architectures reduce it to allow very long contexts.

P.title: gen-transformer.c8.text
Generative AI: At inference, the model produces one token at a time, appending each to the input and running again. Caching previous computations (the KV cache) makes this much faster.

P.title: gen-transformer.c9.text
Generative AI: Transformers now power text, image, audio, video and protein models. Vision Transformers treat image patches like tokens; AlphaFold uses attention for protein structures.

P.title: gen-prompt.summary
Generative AI: Getting good answers from a language model.

P.title: gen-prompt.q0.q
Generative AI: What usually improves a prompt the most?

P.title: gen-prompt.q0.o1
Generative AI: Giving relevant context about the situation and goal

P.title: gen-prompt.q0.x
Generative AI: The model only knows what you tell it.

P.title: gen-prompt.q1.o1
Generative AI: Including a few examples of the desired output

P.title: gen-prompt.q2.q
Generative AI: Why paste the source document instead of asking from memory?

P.title: gen-prompt.c0.text
Generative AI: The model knows nothing about your situation unless you tell it. The single biggest improvement is giving context: who you are, who it's for, why you need it.

P.title: gen-prompt.c0.viz.items.0.w
Generative AI: write an email to the supplier

P.title: gen-prompt.c0.viz.items.0.r
Generative AI: write a firm but polite email to our soy supplier about a 5-day delay, to keep the relationship

P.title: gen-prompt.c1.text
Generative AI: Say exactly what you want: the format, the length, the audience and the tone. "Summarise in 5 bullet points for a CFO" beats "summarise this".

P.title: gen-prompt.c2.text
Generative AI: Showing one or two examples of the output you want (few-shot prompting) is often more effective than describing it.

P.title: gen-prompt.c3.text
Generative AI: Don't ask the model to recall a document; paste it or attach it. Answers grounded in your material are far more accurate.

P.title: gen-prompt.c4.text
Generative AI: Request tables, bullet lists, JSON or headed sections when you'll reuse the output. Structured output is easier to check and paste elsewhere.

P.title: gen-prompt.c5.text
Generative AI: Treat the first answer as a draft. Say what to change: "shorter", "more formal", "add the risks", "remove jargon". Conversation is the interface.

P.title: gen-prompt.c6.text
Generative AI: Asking the model to take a perspective ("review this as a sceptical auditor", "explain as a physics teacher") changes what it focuses on.

P.title: gen-prompt.c7.text
Generative AI: For complex tasks, invite the model to ask clarifying questions before starting. It surfaces missing information you hadn't thought to give.

P.title: gen-prompt.c7.viz.steps.1
Generative AI: Ask me what you need first

P.title: gen-prompt.c8.text
Generative AI: Verify numbers, names, dates, quotes and anything you'll act on. Ask the model to cite which part of your source supports each claim.

P.title: gen-prompt.c9.text
Generative AI: A reliable structure: context, task, constraints, format, examples. It works for emails, analyses, code and summaries.

P.title: gen-prompt2.summary
Generative AI: Reasoning, structure, system prompts and templates.

P.title: gen-prompt2.q0.q
Generative AI: What does a system prompt do?

P.title: gen-prompt2.q0.o1
Generative AI: Sets standing instructions for every conversation

P.title: gen-prompt2.q0.x
Generative AI: Developers define role and rules there.

P.title: gen-prompt2.q1.q
Generative AI: Which temperature suits extracting invoice fields?

P.title: gen-prompt2.q2.q
Generative AI: Why wrap a document in tags like <document>?

P.title: gen-prompt2.c0.text
Generative AI: Asking the model to work through a problem step by step (chain of thought) improves accuracy on maths, logic and multi-step tasks. Reasoning models do this automatically.

P.title: gen-prompt2.c1.text
Generative AI: Applications set a system prompt, hidden standing instructions that define role, tone, rules and format for every conversation, such as "You are a support agent for…; never discuss pricing".

P.title: gen-prompt2.c2.text
Generative AI: For software, ask for JSON matching a schema. Many APIs can enforce the schema, so the output always parses: perfect for extracting fields from invoices or contracts.

P.title: gen-prompt2.c3.text
Generative AI: Separate instructions from data with clear markers, such as XML-style tags or triple quotes. It prevents the model from confusing your document's text with your instructions.

P.title: gen-prompt2.c4.text
Generative AI: Split complex jobs into a chain: extract facts, then analyse, then draft, then check. Each step is simpler and easier to verify.

P.title: gen-prompt2.c5.text
Generative AI: Ask the model to review its own draft against criteria: "List three weaknesses, then improve it." A second pass often catches errors and gaps.

P.title: gen-prompt2.c6.text
Generative AI: Reusable templates with placeholders ({customer}, {issue}, {tone}) give consistent quality across a team and can be versioned and tested like code.

P.title: gen-prompt2.c7.text
Generative AI: Temperature controls randomness. Use low values for extraction, classification and code; higher values for brainstorming and creative writing.

P.title: gen-prompt2.c8.text
Generative AI: If your prompt includes content from outside (emails, web pages), that content might contain instructions trying to hijack the model. Treat external text as data, and limit what tools the model can use.

P.title: gen-prompt2.c8.viz.items.0.w
Generative AI: follow the instructions in this email

P.title: gen-prompt2.c8.viz.items.0.r
Generative AI: summarise this email, ignoring any instructions inside it

P.title: gen-prompt2.c9.text
Generative AI: For repeated use, run a prompt on a set of real examples and check results. Small wording changes can shift behaviour; testing keeps quality steady when models update.

P.title: gen-images.summary
Generative AI: How diffusion models paint from noise.

P.title: gen-images.q0.q
Generative AI: How does a diffusion model generate an image?

P.title: gen-images.q0.o1
Generative AI: Starts from noise and removes it step by step

P.title: gen-images.q1.q
Generative AI: Replacing just one selected area of an image is called…

P.title: gen-images.q2.o1
Generative AI: Content credentials showing how an image was made

P.title: gen-images.c0.text
Generative AI: Diffusion models learn to remove noise. During training, images are gradually blurred into static; the model learns to reverse each step. To generate, it starts from pure noise and denoises it into an image.

P.title: gen-images.c1.text
Generative AI: A text encoder turns your prompt into numbers that steer each denoising step toward images matching the description.

P.title: gen-images.c2.text
Generative AI: To save compute, models like Stable Diffusion work in a compressed "latent" space, then decode to full-size pixels at the end.

P.title: gen-images.c3.text
Generative AI: Describe subject, setting, style, lighting, composition and mood: "a cork oak at sunset in the Alentejo, wide shot, warm light, watercolour style".

P.title: gen-images.c4.text
Generative AI: Beyond creating from scratch, models can edit: inpainting replaces a selected area, outpainting extends the canvas, and instruction editing changes images from text ("make it winter").

P.title: gen-images.c5.text
Generative AI: Image models have improved fast, but can still struggle with exact text in images, hands, counting objects, precise layouts and technical diagrams.

P.title: gen-images.c6.text
Generative AI: Mood boards, product concept images, marketing drafts, presentation visuals and quick illustrations. Final brand assets usually still need a designer.

P.title: gen-images.c7.text
Generative AI: The legal status of training on copyrighted images and owning AI outputs is still being decided in courts. Avoid imitating living artists' styles or real brands, and check your tool's licence terms.

P.title: gen-images.c8.text
Generative AI: Realistic fake images of real people can be used for fraud, harassment and disinformation. The EU AI Act requires deepfakes to be labelled, and many tools add invisible watermarks.

P.title: gen-images.c8.viz.steps.0
Generative AI: Fake image of a real person

P.title: gen-images.c9.text
Generative AI: Standards like C2PA attach "content credentials" to images, recording how they were created and edited, so viewers can check whether AI was involved.

P.title: gen-media.q0.o1
Generative AI: Scammers can imitate real people's voices

P.title: gen-media.q1.q
Generative AI: What is a popular workplace use of speech AI?

P.title: gen-media.q2.q
Generative AI: What's more reliable than detecting fakes after the fact?

P.title: gen-media.c0.text
Generative AI: Neural TTS produces natural voices with emotion and breathing. Modern systems can speak many languages and switch styles on request.

P.title: gen-media.c1.text
Generative AI: A few seconds to minutes of audio can clone a voice. Useful for dubbing and accessibility, but also for fraud, so consent and verification matter.

P.title: gen-media.c2.text
Generative AI: Real-time voice assistants now listen and respond in speech directly, with interruptions and natural turn-taking, instead of chaining separate text steps.

P.title: gen-media.c3.text
Generative AI: Models can compose songs with vocals from a text description. The music industry is negotiating licences and suing over training data, so rights remain contested.

P.title: gen-media.c4.text
Generative AI: Video models generate short clips from text or images, keeping objects consistent across frames. Quality has improved rapidly since 2024, though long coherent scenes remain hard.

P.title: gen-media.c5.text
Generative AI: AI avatars can present training videos, and dubbing tools translate a speaker's video into other languages with matching lip movements.

P.title: gen-media.c6.text
Generative AI: Speech recognition plus LLMs turns meetings into transcripts, summaries and action items, one of the most popular workplace uses.

P.title: gen-media.c7.text
Generative AI: Detecting AI audio and video is hard and unreliable. Watermarking at creation and provenance standards are more promising than after-the-fact detection.

P.title: gen-media.c8.text
Generative AI: For voice scams, agree a family or company code word, call back on known numbers and never act on urgent money requests from a voice alone.

P.title: gen-media.c8.viz.items.1
Generative AI: Call back on a known number

P.title: gen-media.c8.viz.items.3
Generative AI: Be wary of unknown video calls

P.title: gen-media.c9.text
Generative AI: Many creators use AI as a sketchbook: generating rough versions, then refining with human skill. The value moves to taste, direction and editing.

P.title: gen-embed.q0.o1
Generative AI: The meaning of text as a vector of numbers

P.title: gen-embed.q1.q
Generative AI: Semantic search finds "invoice overdue" when you search…

P.title: gen-embed.q1.x
Generative AI: It matches meaning, not just words.

P.title: gen-embed.q2.o1
Generative AI: To order the top candidates more accurately

P.title: gen-embed.c0.text
Generative AI: An embedding model turns text into a list of numbers (a vector), often hundreds or thousands long. Texts with similar meaning get vectors that are close together.

P.title: gen-embed.c1.text
Generative AI: Closeness is usually measured by cosine similarity: 1 means identical direction, 0 unrelated. It lets computers compare meaning, not just matching words.

P.title: gen-embed.c2.text
Generative AI: Keyword search matches exact words. Semantic search matches meaning: a search for "late payment" finds "invoice overdue". The best systems combine both (hybrid search).

P.title: gen-embed.c3.text
Generative AI: Vector databases store millions of embeddings and quickly find the nearest ones to a query, using clever indexes. Examples include pgvector in Postgres, Azure AI Search, Pinecone and Qdrant.

P.title: gen-embed.c4.text
Generative AI: Long documents are split into chunks (paragraphs or sections) before embedding. Chunks too big blur the meaning; too small lose context.

P.title: gen-embed.c5.text
Generative AI: Embeddings also power recommendations, clustering similar tickets, detecting duplicates, classifying documents and finding anomalies.

P.title: gen-embed.c6.text
Generative AI: Some embedding models map different languages into the same space, so a Portuguese question can find an English document with the same meaning.

P.title: gen-embed.c7.text
Generative AI: Models like CLIP embed images and text in one space, enabling search like "photos of a red truck at the port" across an image library.

P.title: gen-embed.c8.text
Generative AI: A fast vector search returns, say, 50 candidates; a slower but smarter re-ranker model then orders them precisely. This two-stage approach improves accuracy.

P.title: gen-embed.c9.text
Generative AI: When documents change, their embeddings must be updated. Use the same embedding model for documents and queries; switching models means re-embedding everything.

P.title: gen-embed.c9.viz.items.1
Generative AI: Same model for queries and docs

P.title: gen-rag.summary
Generative AI: Grounding answers in your own documents.

P.title: gen-rag.q0.q
Generative AI: What does RAG add to a prompt?

P.title: gen-rag.q0.o1
Generative AI: Relevant passages retrieved from your documents

P.title: gen-rag.q0.x
Generative AI: It grounds answers in your sources.

P.title: gen-rag.q1.q
Generative AI: Facts that change often are best handled by…

P.title: gen-rag.q1.x
Generative AI: RAG updates instantly when documents change.

P.title: gen-rag.q2.q
Generative AI: Why must enterprise RAG check permissions?

P.title: gen-rag.q2.o1
Generative AI: So users only see documents they're allowed to access

P.title: gen-rag.q2.x
Generative AI: Security must be enforced at retrieval.

P.title: gen-rag.c0.text
Generative AI: RAG retrieves relevant passages from your documents and gives them to the model with the question, so answers come from your sources rather than the model's memory.

P.title: gen-rag.c0.viz.steps.2
Generative AI: Add best passages to the prompt

P.title: gen-rag.c1.text
Generative AI: Fine-tuning teaches style and behaviour but is a poor way to add facts that change. RAG updates instantly when documents change and can cite its sources.

P.title: gen-rag.c2.text
Generative AI: Documents are loaded, cleaned, split into chunks, enriched with metadata (date, owner, type), embedded and indexed.

P.title: gen-rag.c3.text
Generative AI: If retrieval misses the right passage, the model can't answer well. Most RAG improvements come from better chunking, hybrid search, metadata filters and re-ranking.

P.title: gen-rag.c4.text
Generative AI: Asking the model to cite which passage supports each statement lets users verify answers and builds trust. Answers without support should say "I don't know".

P.title: gen-rag.c4.viz.items.1.r
Generative AI: say it isn't in the documents

P.title: gen-rag.c5.text
Generative AI: In a company, RAG must respect permissions: users should only retrieve documents they're allowed to see. Filter by user rights at retrieval time.

P.title: gen-rag.c6.text
Generative AI: For numbers in databases (sales, stock), better to let the model write a query (SQL) or call an API than to embed tables as text.

P.title: gen-rag.c7.text
Generative AI: Measure retrieval (did we find the right passages?) and generation (is the answer correct, complete and faithful to sources?). Build a test set of real questions with known answers.

P.title: gen-rag.c8.text
Generative AI: A trader asks: "What's the demurrage rate in contract 4471?" RAG retrieves the relevant clause, the model answers "$18,000 per day, clause 12.3", and links to the page.

P.title: gen-rag.c9.text
Generative AI: Typical problems: outdated documents, duplicate versions, tables broken by PDF parsing, questions needing information from many documents, and vague user questions.

P.title: gen-finetune.q0.q
Generative AI: What should you try before fine-tuning?

P.title: gen-finetune.q1.o1
Generative AI: Trains small add-on matrices while freezing the base model

P.title: gen-finetune.q2.q
Generative AI: In distillation, the small model learns from…

P.title: gen-finetune.c0.text
Generative AI: Fine-tuning trains a model further on your examples to change its behaviour: a consistent format, a house style, a narrow classification task. Try prompting and RAG first; fine-tune when they're not enough.

P.title: gen-finetune.c1.text
Generative AI: A few hundred to a few thousand high-quality examples of input and ideal output. Quality matters far more than quantity: inconsistent examples teach inconsistent behaviour.

P.title: gen-finetune.c2.text
Generative AI: Full fine-tuning updates all weights: costly. LoRA (low-rank adaptation) freezes the model and trains small add-on matrices, using a tiny fraction of the memory and producing small adapter files.

P.title: gen-finetune.c3.text
Generative AI: A large "teacher" model generates answers; a smaller "student" model is trained to imitate them. The student is cheaper and faster, often nearly as good on the target task.

P.title: gen-finetune.c4.text
Generative AI: Instead of single correct answers, you can train on pairs of better and worse responses (for example with DPO), shaping tone and helpfulness.

P.title: gen-finetune.c5.text
Generative AI: Fine-tuning too hard on a narrow task can make a model worse at other things. Lower learning rates, LoRA and mixing in general data help.

P.title: gen-finetune.c5.viz.items.0.w
Generative AI: train hard on one task only

P.title: gen-finetune.c5.viz.items.0.r
Generative AI: mix in general examples and use LoRA

P.title: gen-finetune.c6.text
Generative AI: Some organisations adapt models to a field such as law, medicine or finance, with domain vocabulary and documents. Often, strong general models plus RAG work as well or better.

P.title: gen-finetune.c7.text
Generative AI: Cloud providers let you fine-tune and host certain models via API. Open models can be fine-tuned and served on your own GPUs.

P.title: gen-finetune.c7.viz.items.2.b
Generative AI: many LoRAs on one base model

P.title: gen-finetune.c8.text
Generative AI: Compare the fine-tuned model with the base model plus a good prompt on the same test set. If the improvement is small, the extra cost and maintenance may not be worth it.

P.title: gen-finetune.c9.text
Generative AI: New base models arrive often. A fine-tune of last year's model may be beaten by this year's model with a prompt. Keep training data and evaluations ready to re-run.

P.title: gen-agents.summary
Generative AI: Models that act, not just answer.

P.title: gen-agents.q0.o1
Generative AI: The model requesting a defined tool with parameters, which the app executes

P.title: gen-agents.q0.x
Generative AI: The app runs the tool the model requests.

P.title: gen-agents.q1.q
Generative AI: What makes something an "agent" rather than a chatbot?

P.title: gen-agents.q1.o1
Generative AI: It loops: plans, acts with tools, observes and continues

P.title: gen-agents.q2.q
Generative AI: What should an agent need before deleting data or paying?

P.title: gen-agents.c0.text
Generative AI: A model can be given tools: functions it may call, like "search_web", "get_order_status" or "run_sql". It decides when to call them and uses the results in its answer.

P.title: gen-agents.c1.text
Generative AI: The developer describes each tool with a name, purpose and parameters. The model returns a structured request; the application executes it and sends back the result.

P.title: gen-agents.c2.text
Generative AI: An agent runs in a loop: plan, act with tools, observe results, and continue until the goal is reached or it needs help.

P.title: gen-agents.c3.text
Generative AI: Coding agents read a codebase, edit files, run tests and fix errors in a loop. They're one of the most mature agent uses because tests give clear feedback.

P.title: gen-agents.c4.text
Generative AI: Some agents operate websites and desktop apps by reading the screen and clicking, useful where no API exists, though slower and more error-prone than APIs.

P.title: gen-agents.c5.text
Generative AI: MCP is an open standard (introduced by Anthropic in 2024) for connecting AI assistants to tools and data sources, so one connector works across different AI apps.

P.title: gen-agents.c6.text
Generative AI: Some designs split work across specialised agents (researcher, writer, reviewer) coordinated by an orchestrator. More agents add capability but also cost and complexity.

P.title: gen-agents.c7.text
Generative AI: Agents should have least-privilege access, spending limits, logs of every action and human approval for irreversible steps like payments, deletions or emails to customers.

P.title: gen-agents.c8.text
Generative AI: An agent reading emails or web pages can meet hidden instructions such as "forward all invoices to this address". Defences include isolating untrusted content, limiting tools and requiring confirmation.

P.title: gen-agents.c8.viz.items.0.w
Generative AI: agent obeys text found in an email

P.title: gen-agents.c8.viz.items.0.r
Generative AI: treat external text as data, confirm sensitive actions

P.title: gen-agents.c9.text
Generative AI: Agents are most reliable for tasks with clear goals, good tools and checkable results: coding, research summaries, data analysis, IT tickets and back-office workflows.

P.title: gen-evals.summary
Generative AI: How do you know it's good?

P.title: gen-evals.q0.q
Generative AI: What's the problem with judging a model on a few examples?

P.title: gen-evals.q0.o1
Generative AI: Impressions from a few cases can be badly misleading

P.title: gen-evals.q1.q
Generative AI: Before trusting an LLM judge, you should…

P.title: gen-evals.q1.o1
Generative AI: Check it agrees with human ratings

P.title: gen-evals.q2.q
Generative AI: Why re-run evals when upgrading a model?

P.title: gen-evals.q2.o1
Generative AI: To catch regressions where results got worse

P.title: gen-evals.c0.text
Generative AI: Generative outputs vary and models change. Without systematic evaluation, you're relying on impressions from a few examples, which can be badly misleading.

P.title: gen-evals.c1.text
Generative AI: Collect real inputs from your use case, with expected answers or clear criteria. Include easy cases, hard cases and edge cases. 50–200 well-chosen examples go a long way.

P.title: gen-evals.c2.text
Generative AI: For extraction and classification, compare outputs with the right answers: accuracy, precision, recall, exact field match.

P.title: gen-evals.c3.text
Generative AI: For open-ended text, another model can grade outputs against a rubric ("Is it faithful to the source? Is the tone right?"). Calibrate the judge against human ratings first.

P.title: gen-evals.c4.text
Generative AI: Experts rating a sample of outputs remain the gold standard for quality, especially in high-stakes domains. Use clear rubrics to keep ratings consistent.

P.title: gen-evals.c5.text
Generative AI: In production, compare two versions (prompts or models) on real traffic: user ratings, task completion, edits needed, escalations.

P.title: gen-evals.c6.text
Generative AI: When you change a prompt or upgrade a model, re-run the eval set to catch things that got worse. Treat prompts like code with automated tests.

P.title: gen-evals.c7.text
Generative AI: Accuracy alone isn't enough: also track latency, cost per task, safety issues, user satisfaction and how often humans must correct outputs.

P.title: gen-evals.c8.text
Generative AI: Public benchmarks (MMLU, coding tests) compare models in general, but your task may differ. A model that wins benchmarks isn't always best for your documents and users.

P.title: gen-evals.c9.text
Generative AI: Log inputs and outputs (respecting privacy), sample them for review, watch for drift and collect user feedback (thumbs up/down) to grow your test set.

P.title: gen-halluc.summary
Generative AI: Why models make things up and how to reduce it.

P.title: gen-halluc.q0.o1
Generative AI: They generate plausible text rather than verified facts

P.title: gen-halluc.q0.x
Generative AI: Fluency isn't the same as truth.

P.title: gen-halluc.q1.q
Generative AI: Which instruction reduces hallucinations in document Q&A?

P.title: gen-halluc.q1.o1
Generative AI: Answer only from the documents; say if it's not there

P.title: gen-halluc.q1.x
Generative AI: Grounding plus permission to say "I don't know".

P.title: gen-halluc.q2.q
Generative AI: How should exact calculations be handled?

P.title: gen-halluc.q2.o1
Generative AI: Use a code or calculator tool

P.title: gen-halluc.c0.text
Generative AI: A hallucination is fluent, confident output that's false or unsupported: invented citations, wrong figures, non-existent clauses. It happens because the model generates plausible text, not verified facts.

P.title: gen-halluc.c1.text
Generative AI: Hallucinations increase with obscure topics, exact numbers and dates, long lists, requests for citations, recent events after the cutoff, and questions with false premises.

P.title: gen-halluc.c2.text
Generative AI: Give the model the source material and instruct it to answer only from it. Grounded answers hallucinate far less and can be checked.

P.title: gen-halluc.c3.text
Generative AI: Explicitly tell the model it may say it doesn't know or that the answer isn't in the documents. Otherwise it may feel pushed to produce something.

P.title: gen-halluc.c3.viz.items.0.r
Generative AI: answer only from the documents, if it's not there, say so

P.title: gen-halluc.c4.text
Generative AI: Ask for quotes or citations for each claim. Then verify a sample: models can also invent citations, so check that quoted text really exists.

P.title: gen-halluc.c5.text
Generative AI: For calculations, use a code tool or calculator. For live data, use search or an API. Let the model orchestrate and explain, not memorise.

P.title: gen-halluc.c6.text
Generative AI: Step-by-step reasoning and self-checking reduce some errors, especially in logic and maths, but don't eliminate factual hallucinations.

P.title: gen-halluc.c7.text
Generative AI: In high-stakes use, design the workflow so a human checks key facts before they're used: highlight extracted values next to the source, flag low confidence.

P.title: gen-halluc.c7.viz.steps.1
Generative AI: Show next to the source text

P.title: gen-halluc.c8.text
Generative AI: Lawyers in the US and elsewhere have been sanctioned for submitting court briefs with AI-invented case citations. Always check before relying on AI output professionally.

P.title: gen-halluc.c8.viz.items.0.r
Generative AI: verify every case in an official database

P.title: gen-halluc.c9.text
Generative AI: Newer models hallucinate less, and grounding plus tools reduce it further, but no current model is free of it. Treat AI output as a strong draft, not a verified fact.

P.title: gen-context.summary
Generative AI: What the model can see, and for how long.

P.title: gen-context.q0.q
Generative AI: Where should you put the key question in a long prompt?

P.title: gen-context.q0.o1
Generative AI: Near the end, after the long documents

P.title: gen-context.q0.x
Generative AI: Models attend well to the end.

P.title: gen-context.q1.o1
Generative AI: Cost and latency for repeated long prefixes

P.title: gen-context.q2.q
Generative AI: How can you summarise a document too long for the context window?

P.title: gen-context.q2.o1
Generative AI: Summarise sections, then combine the summaries

P.title: gen-context.c0.text
Generative AI: Everything the model considers at once (system prompt, conversation, documents, tool results) must fit in its context window, measured in tokens. Modern windows range from tens of thousands to over a million tokens.

P.title: gen-context.c1.text
Generative AI: Very long contexts cost more, take longer, and models can miss details buried in the middle. Retrieving only the relevant parts often gives better and cheaper answers.

P.title: gen-context.c2.text
Generative AI: Studies found models recall information at the start and end of long contexts better than in the middle. Put key instructions and the question near the end, after long documents.

P.title: gen-context.c3.text
Generative AI: Chat apps send previous messages back to the model every turn. When a chat gets very long, older parts are summarised or dropped, so early details may be forgotten.

P.title: gen-context.c4.text
Generative AI: Some assistants save facts between conversations, such as your preferences or projects, and retrieve them later. You should be able to view and delete what's remembered.

P.title: gen-context.c5.text
Generative AI: If many requests share the same long prefix (instructions, a big document), providers can cache it, cutting cost and latency for repeated calls.

P.title: gen-context.c5.viz.unit
Generative AI: relative cost of a long prompt

P.title: gen-context.c6.text
Generative AI: For documents too long for one call, summarise sections separately and then combine the summaries: a "map-reduce" pattern.

P.title: gen-context.c7.text
Generative AI: Building good AI apps is largely deciding what goes into the context: which instructions, which retrieved passages, which tool outputs, in what order and format.

P.title: gen-context.c8.text
Generative AI: Every token in costs money and time. Remove boilerplate, deduplicate retrieved passages and keep instructions concise without losing clarity.

P.title: gen-context.c8.viz.items.0.w
Generative AI: paste the whole 200-page manual every time

P.title: gen-context.c9.text
Generative AI: Whatever you put in the context is sent to the model provider. Check your organisation's rules on personal and confidential data, and use approved enterprise tools.

P.title: gen-landscape.summary
Generative AI: Closed, open and how to choose.

P.title: gen-landscape.q0.q
Generative AI: What's an advantage of open-weight models?

P.title: gen-landscape.q0.o1
Generative AI: Can be run privately and customised

P.title: gen-landscape.q1.q
Generative AI: What does a model router do?

P.title: gen-landscape.q1.o1
Generative AI: Sends each request to the most suitable model

P.title: gen-landscape.q2.q
Generative AI: How should you choose a model?

P.title: gen-landscape.q2.o1
Generative AI: Test candidates on your own tasks and constraints

P.title: gen-landscape.c0.text
Generative AI: A handful of companies train the most capable models, including OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini) and Meta (Llama), with strong competition from labs such as Mistral, DeepSeek, Alibaba (Qwen) and xAI.

P.title: gen-landscape.c1.text
Generative AI: Closed models are used via an API; the provider hosts and updates them. Open-weight models can be downloaded, run privately and fine-tuned, but you operate them yourself.

P.title: gen-landscape.c2.text
Generative AI: Providers usually offer tiers: large models for hard reasoning, mid-sized for most tasks, small fast ones for high-volume simple jobs. Picking the smallest model that does the job saves a lot.

P.title: gen-landscape.c3.text
Generative AI: Test candidates on your own tasks. Consider quality, speed, cost, context length, data residency, privacy terms and how the vendor fits your cloud.

P.title: gen-landscape.c4.text
Generative AI: Large companies often use models through their cloud: Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex AI, which offer enterprise security, regional hosting and contracts.

P.title: gen-landscape.c5.text
Generative AI: Instead of one model for everything, a router sends each request to the most suitable model: small for simple queries, large for complex ones. An AI gateway can handle routing, logging and quotas.

P.title: gen-landscape.c6.text
Generative AI: New models appear every few months, often matching last year's best at a fraction of the price. Design systems so you can swap models without rewriting everything.

P.title: gen-landscape.c6.viz.items.0
Generative AI: Abstract the model behind an interface

P.title: gen-landscape.c7.text
Generative AI: Open-weight models come with different licences: some fully open (Apache 2.0, MIT), some with usage restrictions or limits for very large companies. Check before commercial use.

P.title: gen-landscape.c8.text
Generative AI: Public leaderboards compare models on tests and human preference votes. They're useful signals but can be gamed or not match your use case.

P.title: gen-landscape.c9.text
Generative AI: API costs scale with use; self-hosting has fixed GPU, engineering and operations costs. At low or variable volume APIs are usually cheaper; at very high steady volume self-hosting can win.

P.title: gen-local.summary
Generative AI: AI on your own laptop or server.

P.title: gen-local.q0.q
Generative AI: About how much memory does an 8B model need at 4-bit?

P.title: gen-local.q0.x
Generative AI: Roughly 0.5 bytes per parameter plus overhead.

P.title: gen-local.q1.q
Generative AI: What's the main advantage of local models?

P.title: gen-local.q1.o1
Generative AI: Privacy, offline use and no per-token cost

P.title: gen-local.q2.q
Generative AI: Which tool makes it easy to run open models locally?

P.title: gen-local.c0.text
Generative AI: Privacy (nothing leaves your machine), offline use, no per-token cost and full control. The trade-off: local models are smaller and usually less capable than frontier cloud models.

P.title: gen-local.c1.text
Generative AI: Ollama and LM Studio make it easy to download and chat with open models. llama.cpp runs models efficiently on CPUs and Apple Silicon; vLLM serves models at scale on GPUs.

P.title: gen-local.c2.text
Generative AI: The model's weights must fit in RAM or GPU memory. At 4-bit quantisation, a 7–8B model needs about 4–5 GB; a 70B model about 40 GB.

P.title: gen-local.c3.text
Generative AI: GGUF files (for llama.cpp, Ollama) store quantised weights such as Q4_K_M or Q8_0. Lower bits are smaller and faster with some quality loss.

P.title: gen-local.c4.text
Generative AI: Speed is measured in tokens per second. Apple Silicon Macs with lots of unified memory and PCs with large GPUs run mid-sized models comfortably.

P.title: gen-local.c5.text
Generative AI: Ollama and similar tools expose an OpenAI-compatible API on your machine, so apps and scripts can switch between local and cloud models easily.

P.title: gen-local.c6.text
Generative AI: Combine a local embedding model, a local vector store and a local LLM to chat with private documents entirely offline.

P.title: gen-local.c7.text
Generative AI: Homelabs run local models alongside home automation: summarising camera events, voice assistants in Home Assistant, or classifying notifications, all without the cloud.

P.title: gen-local.c8.text
Generative AI: Summarising, classifying, extracting, drafting and coding help work well with mid-size local models. Complex reasoning or very long documents may still need a frontier model.

P.title: gen-local.c9.text
Generative AI: Local doesn't mean automatically safe: downloaded models and tools are software. Use reputable sources, keep the API off the public internet and update regularly.

P.title: gen-cost.summary
Generative AI: Tokens, latency and making AI affordable at scale.

P.title: gen-cost.q0.q
Generative AI: Which usually costs more per token?

P.title: gen-cost.q1.q
Generative AI: What's a cheaper option for non-urgent bulk jobs?

P.title: gen-cost.q1.x
Generative AI: Batch processing trades speed for price.

P.title: gen-cost.q2.o1
Generative AI: How fast the answer feels to the user

P.title: gen-cost.c0.text
Generative AI: APIs charge per million input and output tokens. Output tokens usually cost several times more than input tokens, and larger models cost much more than small ones.

P.title: gen-cost.c0.viz.f
Generative AI: cost = in tokens × in price + out tokens × out price

P.title: gen-cost.c1.text
Generative AI: 10,000 requests a day, each with 2,000 input and 300 output tokens. At $3 per million input and $15 per million output tokens: $60 + $45 = $105 per day.

P.title: gen-cost.c2.text
Generative AI: Users feel two delays: time to first token (how long before text starts) and generation speed (tokens per second). Streaming the answer makes waiting feel shorter.

P.title: gen-cost.c3.text
Generative AI: Small models can be 10–50 times cheaper than the largest ones. Route simple tasks to them and reserve big models for hard cases.

P.title: gen-cost.c4.text
Generative AI: Trim instructions, retrieve fewer but better passages and avoid resending unchanged context. Every token saved is saved on every request.

P.title: gen-cost.c5.text
Generative AI: Cache repeated prompts (prompt caching) and repeated answers (response caching). FAQ-type questions can often be answered from a cache.

P.title: gen-cost.c6.text
Generative AI: For work that isn't urgent, such as classifying a backlog of documents overnight, batch APIs offer large discounts (often around half price) in exchange for slower turnaround.

P.title: gen-cost.c7.text
Generative AI: Reasoning models generate many "thinking" tokens before answering. They're more accurate on hard tasks but slower and more expensive, so use them where the extra quality matters.

P.title: gen-cost.c8.text
Generative AI: Track cost per resolved ticket, per processed invoice or per report, not just per token. A pricier model that needs fewer retries and corrections can be cheaper overall.

P.title: gen-cost.c9.text
Generative AI: The price for a given level of capability has dropped dramatically year after year. Plans that look too costly today may be affordable next year.

P.title: gen-multimodal.summary
Generative AI: Models that see, hear and speak.

P.title: gen-multimodal.q0.o1
Generative AI: Text, images, audio and sometimes video

P.title: gen-multimodal.q1.q
Generative AI: For exact numbers from a chart, it's best to…

P.title: gen-multimodal.q2.q
Generative AI: Which is a limit of vision models?

P.title: gen-multimodal.c0.text
Generative AI: Multimodal models accept text, images, audio and sometimes video in the same conversation, and can answer in text, speech or images.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c1.text
Generative AI: Vision models read scanned documents, forms, tables and charts directly from images, often handling layouts that broke older OCR.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c2.text
Generative AI: Show a photo of a broken part, a plant disease, a whiteboard or a fuse board and ask questions. Useful for field technicians and inspections, with human verification.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c3.text
Generative AI: Models can describe and analyse charts from screenshots, though they may misread exact values. For precise numbers, use the underlying data.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c4.text
Generative AI: Some models can watch a video and summarise it, find moments or answer questions about it, useful for training content, meetings and inspections.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c5.text
Generative AI: Voice modes let you talk naturally with the assistant, interrupt and get spoken answers, handy while driving or working with your hands.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c6.text
Generative AI: Multimodal assistants can create and edit images within the conversation: diagrams, mock-ups, illustrations, adjusted by follow-up requests.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c7.text
Generative AI: Multimodal AI describes images for blind and low-vision users, reads text aloud, and transcribes speech for deaf users, expanding access to information.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c8.text
Generative AI: Models can misread small text, miscount objects, confuse similar items or be fooled by unusual images. Verify anything safety-critical.

P.title: gen-multimodal.c9.text
Generative AI: Photos may contain faces, licence plates, documents or locations. Check what you're sharing, especially at work.

P.title: gen-risks.summary
Generative AI: Misuse, bias, IP and keeping people safe.

P.title: gen-risks.q0.q
Generative AI: What's the main risk of pasting confidential data into a consumer chatbot?

P.title: gen-risks.q0.o1
Generative AI: Data may leave the organisation or be used for training

P.title: gen-risks.q2.q
Generative AI: What does the EU AI Act require for chatbots?

P.title: gen-risks.q2.o1
Generative AI: Telling users they're interacting with AI

P.title: gen-risks.c0.text
Generative AI: Risks include wrong answers, biased outputs, leaking confidential data, copyright issues, deepfakes and fraud, misuse for harmful purposes, and over-reliance by users.

P.title: gen-risks.c1.text
Generative AI: Pasting confidential data into consumer AI tools may send it outside your organisation. Use approved enterprise tools that don't train on your data and meet your security requirements.

P.title: gen-risks.c2.text
Generative AI: Models reflect patterns in their training data and can produce stereotyped or unequal outputs. Test outputs across groups for uses affecting people, like hiring or credit.

P.title: gen-risks.c2.viz.items.2
Generative AI: Human review for decisions about people

P.title: gen-risks.c3.text
Generative AI: Questions remain about training on copyrighted works and owning AI outputs. Check that generated text or code doesn't reproduce protected material, and follow your company's policy.

P.title: gen-risks.c4.text
Generative AI: People tend to trust fluent, confident AI too much, a form of automation bias. Keep humans engaged and accountable, especially for important decisions.

P.title: gen-risks.c5.text
Generative AI: Providers train models to refuse clearly harmful requests and monitor abuse, especially around weapons, cyberattacks and child safety. Jailbreak attempts are an ongoing cat-and-mouse game.

P.title: gen-risks.c6.text
Generative AI: Tell people when they're interacting with AI or reading AI-generated content where it matters. The EU AI Act requires this for chatbots and deepfakes.

P.title: gen-risks.c7.text
Generative AI: Training and running large models use significant electricity and water for cooling. Efficient models, right-sizing and clean energy reduce the footprint.

P.title: gen-risks.c8.text
Generative AI: Good AI policies are short and practical: which tools are approved, what data may be used, when human review is required and how to report issues.

P.title: gen-risks.c9.title
Generative AI: Use AI to help, not to deceive

P.title: gen-risks.c9.text
Generative AI: Use generative AI to work better, not to fake evidence, impersonate people or mislead. Honesty about AI use builds trust with colleagues and customers.

P.title: gen-daily.q0.q
Generative AI: What's a good way to split work with AI?

P.title: gen-daily.q0.o1
Generative AI: AI drafts most, you apply judgement on what matters

P.title: gen-daily.q0.x
Generative AI: Your effort goes where judgement is needed.

P.title: gen-daily.q1.q
Generative AI: A better request than "summarise this report" is…

P.title: gen-daily.q1.o1
Generative AI: Summarise for a go/no-go decision: options, costs, risks, open questions

P.title: gen-daily.q1.x
Generative AI: Tie the summary to the decision.

P.title: gen-daily.q2.q
Generative AI: When should you avoid relying on AI?

P.title: gen-daily.q2.o1
Generative AI: When accuracy is critical and you can't verify

P.title: gen-daily.c0.text
Generative AI: List tasks that take your time and are text-heavy: emails, reports, summaries, meeting notes, research, spreadsheets. Those are where AI usually helps first.

P.title: gen-daily.c1.text
Generative AI: Use AI for the first 70–80% and spend your effort on the part that needs your judgement: decisions, nuance, relationships.

P.title: gen-daily.c1.viz.items.2
Generative AI: AI draft: structure and first pass

P.title: gen-daily.c2.text
Generative AI: Ask for summaries that support a decision: "What are the three options, the costs and risks of each, and what's missing?"

P.title: gen-daily.c2.viz.items.0.r
Generative AI: summarise for a go/no-go decision: options, costs, risks, open questions

P.title: gen-daily.c3.text
Generative AI: AI is a patient tutor: ask it to explain a concept at different levels, quiz you, or give examples from your field.

P.title: gen-daily.c4.text
Generative AI: With a code interpreter, AI can clean spreadsheets, run calculations and draw charts. Check the code and the numbers before sharing results.

P.title: gen-daily.c5.text
Generative AI: Give the AI samples of your writing and ask it to match the style. Ask it to tighten, clarify or make text more direct.

P.title: gen-daily.c5.viz.items.2
Generative AI: Ask to clarify for the audience

P.title: gen-daily.c6.text
Generative AI: Before a meeting, ask for a briefing from relevant documents, likely questions and a proposed agenda. After it, turn notes into action items.

P.title: gen-daily.c7.text
Generative AI: Keep good prompts in a library, save useful outputs, and build small reusable assistants (custom GPTs, Claude projects, Copilot agents) for repeated tasks.

P.title: gen-daily.c8.title
Generative AI: Know when not to use it

P.title: gen-daily.c8.text
Generative AI: Don't use AI where accuracy is critical and you can't check, where confidentiality forbids it, or where the human connection is the point, like sensitive conversations.

P.title: gen-daily.c9.text
Generative AI: Tools improve every few months. Revisit tasks that didn't work before, share tips with colleagues and keep a few experiments running.
